title: ～てみる
shortExplanation: A grammar structure used to express the action of trying or attempting something to see what happens.
longExplanation: The 〜てみる grammar point is used with a verb in the 〜て form followed by みる. It emphasizes doing something as a trial or to see the result. It often translates as 'to try doing something' or 'try it out'.

examples.jp: 彼は走ってみたが、まだ膝が痛いと感じた。
examples.romaji: Kare wa hashitte mita ga, mada hiza ga itai to kanjita.
examples.en: He tried running, but he still felt pain in his knee.

examples.jp: 彼女は料理を作ってみたが、失敗してしまった。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa ryouri o tsukutte mita ga, shippai shite shimatta.
examples.en: She tried cooking but ended up failing.

examples.jp: 初めてのデートで、彼は彼女にサプライズをしようと考え、歌ってみた。
examples.romaji: Hajimete no deeto de, kare wa kanojo ni sapuraizu o shiyou to kangae, utatte mita.
examples.en: On their first date, he thought of surprising her and tried singing.

examples.jp: このケーキは美味しそうだから、味見に食べてみる。
examples.romaji: Kono keeki wa oishisou dakara, ajimi ni tabete miru.
examples.en: Since this cake looks delicious, I will try tasting it.
